headline: A random-number flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard wallets fueled an $88 million Bitcoin heist as OpenAI teased Astra, a model whose math breakthroughs sharpen fears of AI-driven cryptanalysis.

emerging_trends.text: A random-number generator bug baked into Coinkite's Coldcard firmware in March 2021 let thieves sweep thousands of Bitcoin wallets in minutes, proof that one entropy mistake can quietly doom hardware marketed as the safest place to hold coins.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Coldcard Wallet RNG Flaw Drives $88 Million Bitcoin Heist

emerging_trends.text: OpenAI's unreleased Astra model has already produced ten original advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science, deepening the worry that frontier systems will soon crack the number theory underpinning modern cryptography.
emerging_trends.topic_title: OpenAI Teases Astra Model After Math Breakthroughs

emerging_trends.text: Defenders are racing to fence in AI coding agents that inherit their users' full permissions, and the open-source Nono sandbox aims to stop a prompt injection or a hallucinated command from reaching credentials and production systems.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Nono Sandbox Aims to Contain Autonomous AI Agents

topics.title: Coldcard Wallet RNG Flaw Drives $88 Million Bitcoin Heist
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer raised the tally to roughly $88.6 million and pinned the losses on the flawed random number generator, which produced predictable seeds across thousands of wallets.
topics.summary: Coinkite's Coldcard, a Bitcoin-only hardware wallet from the Canadian maker, shipped a March 2021 firmware integration error that routed seed generation to a deterministic software pseudorandom number generator, letting attackers predict private keys and empty wallets; Galaxy Research mapped a July 30 sweep that drained 1,196 addresses in 41 minutes, and owners who generated seeds on affected firmware should move funds to a freshly seeded wallet.

sources.title: COLDCARD wallet RNG flaw likely linked to $88 million Bitcoin theft
Coldcard Hardware Wallet Flaw Linked to $70 Million Bitcoin Theft in 41 Minutes

topics.title: Atomic macOS Stealer Infection Dissected
topics.latest_developments: The SANS Internet Storm Center published a hands-on analysis of an Atomic macOS Stealer infection on August 2, 2026.
topics.summary: Atomic macOS Stealer, sold as malware-as-a-service, harvests browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and keychain secrets from Mac users and typically spreads through malvertising and cracked-app installers; Mac owners should install software only from trusted sources.

topics.title: OpenAI Teases Astra Model After Math Breakthroughs
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI unveiled Astra, an unreleased model built for complex, long-running tasks, after an internal version produced ten significant advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science.
topics.summary: Frontier labs increasingly ship models that solve original mathematics, a capability that shadows cryptography after Anthropic's Claude Mythos derived a fatal attack on the HAWK post-quantum signature scheme; Astra's math results sharpen questions about AI-driven cryptanalysis and the pace of offensive capability gains.

sources.title: OpenAI teases Astra, its next major AI model, after it solves 10 long-standing math problems

topics.title: Nono Sandbox Aims to Contain Autonomous AI Agents
topics.latest_developments: Luke Hinds and Stephen Parkinson launched Nono through their startup nolabs, an open-source sandbox that isolates AI coding agents from the systems their users can reach.
topics.summary: AI coding agents run with their users' permissions, reaching sensitive files, credentials, and production systems, where a prompt injection or hallucinated command can escalate into an incident; Nono sandboxes those agents to contain the blast radius.

topics.title: Chrome to Block New Tab Hijacker Extensions
topics.latest_developments: Google is preparing a Chrome feature that blocks policy-installed extensions from hijacking the New Tab page or switching the default search engine by default.
topics.summary: Enterprise policy-installed extensions have long forced New Tab and default-search changes on users; the coming Chrome protection curbs that abuse and hands control back to administrators and users.

sources.title: Google Chrome may soon block New Tab hijacker extensions by default

business_politics.title: Trump Calls Off Iran Strike as Talks Resume
business_politics.latest_developments: Trump said U.S.-Iran talks will restart after he canceled Saturday's planned attack, and Tehran told mediators it is near a deal with Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping, sending oil prices lower.
business_politics.summary: President Trump scrapped a planned U.S. strike on Iran late Saturday, saying Gulf states pressed him toward negotiation and that mediators sketched the outlines of a deal to end the six-month war; crude fell on the de-escalation as Tehran signaled openness to reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

business_politics.title: AstraZeneca in $400 Billion Talks With Bristol Myers Squibb
business_politics.latest_developments: AstraZeneca opened talks with Bristol Myers Squibb over a roughly $400 billion combination that would create the world's fourth-largest drugmaker by market value.
business_politics.summary: AstraZeneca, the British pharmaceutical giant, is discussing a tie-up worth about $400 billion with New York-based Bristol Myers Squibb; a completed deal would rank among the largest pharmaceutical mergers ever and reorder the industry's competitive landscape.

sources.title: AstraZeneca holds talks with Bristol Myers Squibb over $400bn tie-up

business.latest_developments: Writing in TribLive, Barāta A. Bey argued minority-owned businesses grow through better access to capital and urged policymakers to expand credit for entrepreneurs.
business.summary: In a TribLive opinion piece, Barāta A. Bey contended that success for minority-owned businesses starts with an idea, determination, and access to capital, calling on lawmakers to widen entrepreneurs' access to credit.

business.title: Highland Park Victorian Sits on Its Own Block
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Magazine's Hot Property featured a 1923 brick Victorian at 5454 Wellesley Avenue in Highland Park that occupies its own dedicated parcel.
business.summary: A brick Victorian built in 1923 at 5454 Wellesley Avenue in Pittsburgh's Highland Park neighborhood stands on an unusual parcel that gives the house a full block to itself, a quirk left by the original subdivision.

sources.title: This Highland Park Home Has Its Own Block

around_town.title: Mount Lebanon Tables E-Bike Restrictions
around_town.latest_developments: Mount Lebanon commissioners tabled a proposed ordinance to restrict e-bike use in the South Hills municipality, sending the plan back for revision.
around_town.summary: Mount Lebanon's commissioners set aside an ordinance meant to crack down on e-bikes in the South Hills community, returning the measure to the drawing board after debate over its restrictions.

around_town.title: Flash Flood Warning Hits Western Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: Forecasters escalated Sunday's Flood Watch to a Flash Flood Warning as downpours dropped up to three inches, a water main broke in the Strip District, muddy water rushed down a Cranberry Township hillside, and Kennywood closed early.
around_town.summary: Heavy rain of up to three inches triggered a Flash Flood Warning across Western Pennsylvania on August 2, sending muddy water down a hillside in Cranberry Township, Butler County, bursting a water main that flooded a road in Pittsburgh's Strip District, and forcing Kennywood Park to shut down early.

sources.title: Flash Flood Warning, Flood Watch in place for Western Pa.

around_teams.title: Steelers Cut Savage, Sign Safety Jenkins
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers released former first-round safety Darnell Savage and signed 10th-year veteran Rayshawn Jenkins, and the Post-Gazette reported the team still hunting safety help behind Jaquan Brisker and DeShon Elliott.
around_teams.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers cut Darnell Savage, a former Green Bay first-round pick, and added free-agent safety Rayshawn Jenkins, a 10-year veteran who spent last season with the Cleveland Browns, as coaches keep searching for depth alongside Jaquan Brisker and DeShon Elliott.
